blocks.text: **Caramel** stands for « **Création Assistée de Ressources et d'Activités Magistère et Éléa** » (AI-assisted creation of resources and activities for Magistère and Éléa): it's an **activity-creation workshop**, made **by teachers, for teachers**, **designed first and foremost for Éléa and Magistère** — but it also works for **Moodle**. You describe what you want, an AI prepares the content, you check and adjust it, then you get a file ready to upload.
Our philosophy: you stay in control
The AI is an **assistant**, but **you are the one who decides**. At every moment:

items: **Before**: you set the teaching framework by filling in the description fields.
**During**: the content generated by the AI is **fully editable** in the editor, to fine-tune it to your intent.
**After**: even once the file is downloaded, you can still **open and edit it** elsewhere if needed — nothing is locked, it's yours.

blocks.text: Your data is protected
Caramel is designed so that **no teaching data is ever exposed**. Here, in plain terms, is what stays with you and what travels — and where.

items: **Your documents stay on your computer.** When you drop a file (PDF, image…) in advanced mode, the text is extracted **entirely in your browser**: nothing is sent to a server.

**What does travel stays hosted in France.** Your generation requests go through **shared university servers** (the **ILaaS** project); voice (microphone or audio file) is transcribed by **Albert**, the **DINUM's sovereign service**. Neither one **collects nor resells** your data — and **the audio is not kept**.
**Copying and pasting to an external AI is on you.** If you copy a prompt to use it in a third-party service, the protection of your data then depends on **that service's terms**.

blocks.text: The journey is always the same: **describe → choose → generate → check → download**. It's detailed in the following chapters. To reopen this tutorial, click **“Tutorial”** at the top right.
Everything starts here. **The clearer your description, the more relevant the result.** Two ways to express yourself, depending on whether you prefer to move fast or frame things precisely.
Quick mode
Ideal for getting to the point. You fill in **two fields**:

items: **Who are you?** — your subject and the level of your students (e.g. "biology teacher, Year 8").
**What do you want to create?** — the topic and the type of exercise you want (e.g. "a quiz on digestion").

blocks.alt: Quick mode: two fields to describe who you are and what you want to create.

blocks.text: Advanced mode

For a more structured request. This mode offers **precise fields** (subject, level, theme, number of questions, specific instructions…) and lets you **attach a document** or **import a web page** as a starting point.

blocks.alt: Advanced mode with its detailed fields: subject, level, theme, documents.

blocks.text: If you leave the "documents" area empty, the AI will rely **solely on its general knowledge**. By dropping your lesson in there, you force it to **stick to your content** — it's your choice.
The little bonus: grounding in the official curriculum

When you fill in the **subject**, the **topic** and the **level**, Caramel can **ground the generation in the official French school curriculum** (Éduscol), according to the relevant cycle. The content produced then aligns more closely with what your class is expected to learn.

In plain terms, a **RAG** ("retrieval-augmented generation") is a **reference library** in which the AI **looks up the right excerpts** before writing — here, the official curriculum — rather than answering from memory. The result: activities better aligned with the curriculum.

This grounding is **automatic and non-blocking**: if you specify neither subject nor level, generation still works, simply without this curriculum reference. Providing this information costs nothing and improves the result.
Once your need is described, the **activity tiles** become clickable. Each tile corresponds to a type of exercise. Click the one that suits you.

blocks.alt: The grid of activity tiles available in Caramel.

blocks.text: Two main families

head: Family
What it is
Formats produced
rows: **Interactive** activities: multiple choice, True/False, fill-in-the-blanks, drag and drop, crosswords, flashcards, glossary, course presentation, interactive book, interactive video…
Activities and resources for these platforms: Quiz, multiple choice, Matching, Millionaire, Page, Book, Glossary, Assignment…

blocks.text: The tiles only become active **once the description is filled in** at step 1. If a tile stays greyed out, go back and describe your need (or ask Caramélia to do it).

**H5P** is an **open, free standard** for interactive activities, used everywhere in education (Moodle, Éléa, Magistère, La Sucrerie…). Caramel bundles the **official H5P libraries** for each activity type: the files produced are therefore **100% compatible** with these platforms.

**Moodle** is the engine behind the online course platforms of the French national education system: **Éléa** and **Magistère** are built on it. That's why Caramel can also produce Moodle-specific formats — a **.mbz backup**, or **.xml / GIFT questions** for a question bank.

Not sure which type to pick? The **filters** at the top of the grid (by platform, by theme) narrow the list, and each tile's name describes the exercise it produces. Caramélia can also advise you on the most suitable type.
After clicking a tile, a window opens. This is where **you ask the AI for the content**. Two options, depending on the level of control you want.
Option A — Generate in one click
The fast track. Click **"Generate in one click"**: Caramel sends your request to the AI and fills in the activity all by itself. Within seconds, the content is ready to preview.

blocks.alt: The simple view with the Generate in one click button.

blocks.text: The small **arrow** to the right of the button lets you **choose the AI model** (a fast one, a more powerful one…). By default, a good model is already selected: no need to touch it to get started well. It's yet another example of how **you stay in control**.
Option B — Use an external AI
For maximum control. Caramel displays the **prompt** (the instruction meant for the AI), which you can read, edit and use elsewhere.

items: **Copy the prompt** provided (copy button).
**Paste it into the AI of your choice** (for example Le Chat by Mistral, or another assistant).
**Get the response** and **paste it** into Caramel.
Caramel automatically **checks and repairs** the content before using it.

blocks.alt: The guided view with the prompt to copy into an external AI.

blocks.text: A **prompt** is simply the instruction message you give to an AI. Caramel writes it for you; it's up to you to adjust it if you wish.
Lots of questions? Caramel handles it

For an activity with **many items** (for example a quiz of 20 or 30 questions), Caramel **automatically splits the work into several steps** and shows a **progress bar**. For you, it stays **a single click** — but without this trick, such a large request might break off partway through.
During a step-by-step generation, **let Caramel finish** (the progress bar shows it) before previewing. The result is a complete quiz, cleanly merged.
Once the content is generated, **take the time to check it** in the preview window. The activity behaves there exactly as it will for your students.

items: **Do the exercise yourself**: click the answers, drag the labels, fill in the blanks.
**Check the feedback**: do the correct answers and explanations display properly?
**Review the text**: spelling, formulas, images — is everything in line with what you intended?

blocks.alt: The preview window: the activity is tested directly in the simulator.

blocks.text: This window is a **simulator**: it mimics the final rendering without sending anything anywhere. You can test it as many times as needed.

A detail to fix? No need to regenerate everything: switch to **editing** (next chapter) to adjust it by hand. You can also relaunch a generation if the result doesn't suit you. **You are the one who validates.**
Want to change a question, a word, an image? Click **"Edit"** (pencil icon): a **visual editor** opens, where every field of the activity can be changed directly, without re-importing anything.

blocks.alt: The editing menu: fine-tune the content down to the smallest detail.

blocks.text: Format the text
The fields that allow it show a **toolbar** when you click inside them: bold, italic, lists, etc. The formatting is kept in the final activity.
Insert mathematical formulas
For science subjects, you can add **clean, readable mathematical formulas** directly in the relevant fields. An assistant helps you compose them without knowing the technical language (LaTeX).
Words to find (drag, mark, complete)
For the **Drag the Words**, **Mark the Words** or **Fill in the Blanks** activities, you designate the target words right within the text: the editor turns them into blanks or labels.
Fill-in-the-blanks of the Éléa Quiz
For the **Fill in the Blanks** questions of the Quiz activity (Éléa), a dedicated editor makes it easy to create the gaps to complete and their accepted answers.
Add your images
Some activities accept **your own images**: drag them into the intended field (cards, items to sort, background image…). They are embedded directly in the final file.
Advanced settings
Each activity offers **optional settings** (a collapsed section at the bottom of the editor): number of attempts, showing hints, button behaviour… Worth exploring once the essentials are in place.
After each change, **go back and preview** the activity to check the rendering. The back-and-forth between editing and previewing is the best way to get a perfect result.
Happy with your activity? All that's left is to **grab it**. The download menu offers several formats, arranged in families.

blocks.alt: The action bar: download (H5P, DOCX, ODT, PDF), share "To La Sucrerie", or edit.

head: Family
Formats
What it's for
rows: Import the **interactive** activity into Éléa, Magistère or Moodle. This is the main option.
Get a **text** version to print or edit. The mathematical formulas remain editable.
A fixed version, perfect for printing or handing out.

blocks.text: The **.h5p** format is the most versatile: it's the one that keeps all the interactivity and opens everywhere (Éléa, Magistère, Moodle, La Sucrerie).

In a **Word / PDF** version, highly interactive activities are necessarily **simplified** (a drag-and-drop becomes a fill-in list, for example): that's normal — the original **interactive format** keeps the full mechanics.

Want to **share** your creation with other teachers? The **"To La Sucrerie"** button (to the right of the formats) publishes it to Caramel's twin library — see the bonus chapter "Share on La Sucrerie".

Once the file is downloaded, here's how to add it to your course. The procedure depends on the file's **format**. The screenshots below show the Éléa example (the process is very similar on Magistère and Moodle).
.h5p file (interactive activity)

items: In your course, **turn on editing mode**.
**Add an activity** of type **H5P** (or "Interactive Content").
**Drop the .h5p file** into the intended area, then **save**.

blocks.alt: Adding an H5P activity in an Éléa course.

blocks.text: .mbz file (Moodle backup)
This format adds one or more activities to your course **without overwriting** the existing ones, via the **restore** tool.

items: Open your course, then **"Restore"** (backup / restore menu).
**Load the .mbz file**, then choose **"Merge"** with the current course.
Go through the proposed steps up to the confirmation.

blocks.alt: Restoring a .mbz file in Éléa — uploading the file.
Restoring a .mbz file in Éléa — merging with the course.

blocks.text: .xml file (Glossary)
To import a list of definitions into a **glossary**: create a glossary in the course, then use its **"Import entries"** option and select the .xml file.

blocks.alt: Importing entries into an Éléa glossary from an XML file.

blocks.text: .xml and .GIFT files (question bank)
To add questions to your **question bank**: from the bank, choose **"Import"**, select the format (Moodle XML or GIFT) and load the file.

blocks.alt: Importing questions into the Éléa question bank.

blocks.text: .html file (page content)
To insert content directly into a **text area**: open the area's editor, switch to **"source code" (HTML)** mode, then paste the file's content.

blocks.alt: Pasting HTML in source code mode into an Éléa page.

blocks.text: The **.h5p** format is the simplest to integrate and the most common. When in doubt, go for it.

Proud of your activity? **Publish it on La Sucrerie**, Caramel's twin library, so that other teachers can find and reuse it. It all starts from the **"To La Sucrerie"** button in the download menu (step 6).

blocks.alt: The pink "To La Sucrerie" button in the download bar.

blocks.text: **La Sucrerie** is a big shared cupboard of activities, **free and reusable** (Creative Commons licence). **Caramel is for creating**, **La Sucrerie for sharing and finding** — the two speak the same language.
How it works

items: Click **"To La Sucrerie"** (the pink button, to the right of the download formats).
An **AI prepares the record** for you (about 15 seconds): title, description, objectives, keywords, subject and level.
**Check and correct** this pre-filled record, then enter your **name** (shown as the author) and your **academic email address**.
Tick the **licence** box then **confirm**: an automatic check reviews the content, and the activity is published to the catalogue.

blocks.text: The **publication name** is displayed as the author of the activity: by default your **first and last name**, but you are perfectly free to choose a **pseudonym**. Your **email**, on the other hand, stays **private** (encrypted, never displayed) — it is only used to send you a **management link** to edit or remove the activity later.

**Submitting** means publishing your activity in the public catalogue. The AI **suggests** the information to file it neatly, but **you stay in charge**: everything remains editable before you confirm, and nothing is published without your consent.
You keep control even after publication: the **management link** received by email lets you **edit or remove** your activity whenever you wish.

You now know the whole journey — here's a **shortcut**. **Caramélia** is Caramel's **mascot**: the **site's logo**, which we wanted to **give a human touch**. She is also your **assistant**, able to carry out **all the previous steps for you**. You'll find her at the **bottom right of the screen**; one click opens a **chat window** where you write to her as you would to a colleague.

blocks.alt: The Caramélia window open, with its welcome message and the "Help with the site" and "Create an activity" buttons.

blocks.text: She can do two things

items: **Answer your questions** about Caramel ("How do I add a file to Éléa?", "What is a fill-in-the-blanks text?", "What happens to my data?").
**Help you create**: describe your need in plain language ("a 10-question quiz on fractions for Year 6") and she **prepares everything for you**.

blocks.text: Concretely, Caramélia **does not build the activity herself**: she **fills in the fields and opens the right tile for you**, exactly as if you were doing it by hand. The result is therefore identical to what you'd get without her — she just saves you time.
Several activities in one go

This is one of her great strengths. Ask for example **"a quiz and flashcards on the water cycle"**: Caramélia shows a **checklist** of the activities she suggests. You tick the ones you're interested in, you confirm, and she **launches all the generations one after another**.
At the end of a batch of several activities, a **"Download a ZIP"** button gathers all the files at once. Ideal for preparing a whole teaching sequence in a few minutes.
Give her a starting document

A **paperclip** (or a simple drag and drop) lets you attach a **document or an image** (PDF, Word, slideshow, photo…). Caramélia extracts the text from it to use as a base — handy for turning an existing lesson into exercises. You can also **talk** to her using the microphone.

**You stay in charge, even with Caramélia.** Before each generation, she shows a **summary** (who, what, level, number of questions, chosen activities) with three buttons: **Launch**, **Change activity**, **Cancel**. **Nothing goes out without your confirmation.**

To answer accurately, Caramélia relies on a **document base** (a "RAG"): instead of improvising, she **draws reliable excerpts** from Caramel's documentation and uses the exact labels of the buttons you see on screen. (The **RAG** is also what makes it possible to ground the generation in the official curriculum — see the step "Describe your need".)
Caramel is a **living** project, and your opinion matters. A **discussion room** brings together the teachers who use Caramel on **Tchap**, the French State's secure messaging service.
What is this room for?

items: **Ask your questions** and get help with creating, editing or integrating into your courses.
**Report an issue** or suggest an improvement.
**Discover what's new**: Caramel's updates are announced there.
**Share your practices** with other colleagues.

blocks.text: **Tchap** is the official messaging service of the French administration, reserved for State employees. You log in with your professional address, without creating a new account.
The link to the room is also available at the top of every page, next to the "Tutorial" button. And for a quick question, **Caramélia** answers directly in the app.
Frequently asked questions

items: **How does the AI generate its content?** You describe your need; Caramel turns it into a **precise instruction** for the AI, enriched with the **official curricula** (the RAG), then sends it to an **AI hosted in France** (ILaaS) that drafts the content. Caramel **checks and fixes** it before filling the activity — and **you** review and adjust.

**Does it work on Moodle?** Yes. Caramel produces **standard formats** (**.h5p**, **.mbz**, **.xml / GIFT**) that **Moodle reads natively**. In fact, **Éléa** and **Magistère** are built on Moodle: what works for them works on any Moodle platform.

**Is my data sent anywhere?** Your texts are only used to generate the activity via the AI; Caramel does not keep your content. Text extraction from your documents and images happens **in your browser**.
**The AI result is imperfect, what should I do?** Adjust it by hand in the editor, or relaunch the generation with a more precise description. You are always the one who validates.
**Can I create several activities at once?** Yes, by asking **Caramélia**: she offers a checklist then groups the files into a ZIP.
**Which format should I choose for Éléa or Magistère?** The **.h5p** in most cases: it's interactive and opens everywhere.

The built-in assistant (candy button) that answers your questions and prepares activities for you.
Ask the AI to prepare the content from your description.
The instruction message given to an AI. Caramel writes it for you.
A reference base from which the AI draws reliable excerpts before answering (here: Caramel's documentation, and the official curriculum).
The French school curriculum (Éduscol) on which the generation can be grounded according to subject and level.
The automatic splitting of a large request (many questions) to avoid cut-offs — transparent to you.
The open standard for interactive activities, readable by Éléa, Magistère and Moodle.
The engine behind the course platforms (Éléa, Magistère). .mbz = backup; .xml / GIFT = questions.
A simple text format for importing questions into a question bank.
Online course platforms of the French national education system, built on Moodle.
The interface that lets you change the activity field by field, without code.
The preview window that mimics the final rendering to test the activity.
The twin library where you **share and find** activities.

blocks.text: A question left unanswered here? Ask **Caramélia**, or the **Tchap room** (previous chapter): the community is there for that.
